newsitem.title: INDIA: TEXT - Proposed amendments in Indian takeover code.
newsitem.headline: TEXT - Proposed amendments in Indian takeover code.

text.p: The following is a summary of changes proposed by market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on takeover of corporates
** The definition of 'persons acting in concert' have been elaborated and certain types of persons has been enlisted who would be presumed to be acting in concert.
** 'Offer period' has been defined so also the 'promoter'.
** To bring about greater transparency and minimise exercise of discretion, circumstances under which the requirement of public offer would be inapplicable has been delineated.
** Preferential allotment has been exempted subject to appropriate checks and balances to protect the interest of the investors.
** To deal with any residual circumstances which might warrant an exemption constitution of a panel has been proposed.
** Elaborate disclosure requirements to monitor change in control and creeping acquisitions have been provided for.
** Threshold for mandatory public offer has been retained at 10 percent.

** Consolidation of holdings at the rate of 2.0 percent in any 12-month period between the buyer acquirer who holds not less than 10 percent but not more than 25 percent and at the rate of 5.0 percent in any 12-month period between 25-50 percent holding has been provided for. Acquisitions exceeding this rate wilt attract public offer requirement.
** Takeovers have not been defined but change in control made a ground for public offer.
** Merchant bankers have been given greater responsiblity. The procedure for public announcement and the content of public announcement have been elaborated and clarified.
** Conditional offer has been permitted subject to several checks and balances to prevent previous frivolous offers and disruption of market.
** Acquisitions by an acquirer during the offer period have been permitted subject to the condition that highest price paid by the acquirer should also be paid to the share-holders.

** Vetting of the letter of SEBI has been replaced by filling. The requirement of record rate this been changed to a specified date at the option of the acqurier. This will reduce the length of the period required for the completion of the offer.

** The provision of minimum offer price which now exist has been retained. In addition preferential offers made to the acquirer and the highest price paid by the acquirer during an offer period and average price of this acquisition in the 12-month preceding to offer would also be reconked.
** Besides cash offer and exchange offer, payment of considerations through any other securities at the option of the investor has been allowed.
** The requirement of minimum shareholdings after the offer has been modified and 100 percent offer now be possible.

** Escrow accounts at 10 percent of the consideration of the offer has been made mandatory with provisions for forfeiture. This will impose discipline on deliquent acquirers to complete for the offer on time and prevent frivolous offers. At the same time to ensure that the condition does not become too onerous on the acquirers, escrow account would be allowed also in the form of bank guarantees of securities with appropriate margin.
** Elaborate disclosure requirements in the offer document has been imposed.
** Competitive bid has been defined and the present limit of 14 days as been extended to 21 days.
** Revision of offer has been permitted to include upward revision of price and quantity of shares.
** Grounds for withdraw of offers have been specified with greater clarity.
** Specific obligations have been cast on the target company and acquirers.
** Target company could make recommendations to its shareholders about an offer keeping in view juridical responsibilities of its director.

** Existing penalties has been sought to be stregthened by recommending amendment to SEBI Act to expand the scope of adjudication, amount of monetary penalties, forfeiture of shares acquired in violation of the regulations and their auction. A provision for personal disqualification of directors has also been recommended.
